gap: B: Everything within about 10 m of the camera must hold up at full resolution. The sign base, median planter, kerb and road need textured, weathered surfaces (chipped and grimy concrete, crisp cracks, aggregate and lane paint) with bevelled edges and contact shadows. The planter needs dense, varied plants with self-shadowing. No flat untextured shapes, cut-card foliage or smeared road texture may appear in the bottom third of the frame.

Judge: The commercial-looking frame wins all four pairs, and not narrowly: pair 1 to A, and pairs 2, 3 and 4 to the other side. The test was not truly blind, because every winning frame has a visible "Grand Theft Auto V" logo in the bottom-right corner. I judged on image content alone, but the orchestrator should crop or mask that logo in future pairs. The development game's frames show the same problems every time. First, the median planter at street level is full of blocky, low-poly cut-card plants (pairs 1, 2 and 4). Second, large areas of road have a smeared, blotchy, low-resolution texture. Third, there are flat untextured primitives in the foreground, such as the sign base in pair 1 and the rooftop props in pair 3. Fourth, there is very little life: few vehicles, few pedestrians and no street clutter. Fifth, the skyscrapers are placeholder boxes with tiled window textures. Sixth, haze and depth are weak and the clouds look like cotton sprites. There are also outright bugs: the car drives through the median in pair 2, and the sedan has a clipped specular blob in pair 4. The two gameplay frames also carry a HUD that hurts the cinematic read. Its real strengths are a distinctive Singapore-like setting (shophouse rows with shutters, rain-tree avenues, recognisable skyline landmarks), warm colour grading and a high-quality sedan model, and pair 4 shows it is closest at street level. The reference frames win on believable low-sun lighting with haze and depth, weathered and well-dressed environments, people placed to tell a story, and deliberate hero composition. None of the development frames wow; two of the reference frames do (pair 3 B and pair 4 B). The fix with the most leverage is foreground fidelity: no blocky plants, smeared road or untextured primitives within 10 m of the camera. After that, add traffic, pedestrians and street clutter, and stronger aerial haze.
